prompt:
Feature: declare the permission a route needs on the route itself.

Routes that need one of the user permission flags (can_organize, can_manage, can_invite, can_manage_household) check it inside the handler today, through the controllers' checks helper (OperationChecks). Nothing on the route says it is guarded, so the only way to know which routes need which permission is to read every handler, and a change to who may call a route is easy to miss in review. Each guarded route should declare its permission as a FastAPI dependency, so the whole route-to-permission table can be read back from the app.

Expected:
1. A new module importable as `mealie.routes._base.permissions` (with the other route base helpers, in the package that holds BaseUserController and HttpRepo). It provides:
   - `Perm`, a string enum (each member is a `str` equal to its value) with ANY_VALID_USER ("any_valid_user"), GROUP_ORGANIZE ("group:organize"), GROUP_MANAGE ("group:manage"), GROUP_INVITE ("group:invite") and HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE ("household:manage"). ANY_VALID_USER marks a route as open to any signed-in user on purpose.
   - `RequirePermission`, built from one Perm (`RequirePermission(perm)`), which keeps it on the attribute `perm`. An instance is the dependency itself: called with a user, `RequirePermission(perm)(user)` returns nothing when the user holds the flag the permission maps to, and raises FastAPI's `HTTPException` (fastapi.HTTPException) with status_code 403 when not. GROUP_ORGANIZE maps to can_organize, GROUP_MANAGE to can_manage, GROUP_INVITE to can_invite and HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE to can_manage_household; ANY_VALID_USER lets every user through. Only that one flag decides: `PrivateUser.model_construct(can_organize=True)` (no other field set) passes GROUP_ORGANIZE, the same user with can_organize False is refused, and `PrivateUser.model_construct()` with no fields at all passes ANY_VALID_USER. When FastAPI runs it for a route, that single argument is the signed-in user (what get_current_user resolves).
   - `require(perm)`, the helper a route uses to declare its permission in the route decorator's `dependencies` list; it attaches `RequirePermission(perm)` to that route.
2. The declarations are read back from the app this way: walk `fastapi.routing.iter_route_contexts(app.routes)` (FastAPI includes routers lazily, so app.routes alone lists included routers, not their routes), keep the contexts whose `.route` is an APIRoute, and look at the direct dependencies of each one's dependant (`route.dependant.dependencies`). Every dependency whose `call` is a RequirePermission instance declares its `perm` for each of the route's methods, with the route's full path (including /api). A RequirePermission nested deeper, for example inside a controller class's own dependencies or inside another dependency, is not seen.
3. Read that way, the table must be exactly the following, with nothing else declared anywhere (in this change no route declares GROUP_INVITE or ANY_VALID_USER: the invitation routes keep the can_invite check they make in their handlers):
   - GROUP_ORGANIZE: POST /api/foods, PUT /api/foods/merge, PUT /api/foods/{item_id}, DELETE /api/foods/{item_id}, POST /api/groups/labels/merge, POST /api/organizers/categories, POST /api/organizers/categories/merge, PUT /api/organizers/categories/{item_id}, DELETE /api/organizers/categories/{item_id}, POST /api/organizers/tags, POST /api/organizers/tags/merge, PUT /api/organizers/tags/{item_id}, DELETE /api/organizers/tags/{item_id}, POST /api/organizers/tools/merge.
   - GROUP_MANAGE: POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers, POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/test, GET, PUT and DELETE /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}, POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}/test, GET /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts, PUT and DELETE /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts/{prompt_name}, GET and PUT /api/groups/ai-providers/settings, PUT /api/groups/preferences, GET /api/households/members, PUT /api/households/permissions.
   - HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE: POST and DELETE /api/households/mealplans/ical, PUT /api/households/preferences.
   These are the routes that call the checks helper today, each with the flag it checks now (the two meal plan iCal token routes check it in the token setter they share).
4. Who may call what does not change: on these routes a user without the flag still gets 403 and a user with it is let through, and every other route behaves as before. The handler-side checks this replaces are no longer needed.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/category_tag_tool_tests tests/integration_tests/user_group_tests tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests tests/integration_tests/test_openapi.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
